After: the id pairs (2, 4) and (3, 4) become two new accent edges, B to D and C to D, closing the cycle." width="100%"} A strict bulk version of `add_edge_by_id()` that only accepts integer node IDs — no label resolution. All referenced nodes must already exist in the graph. This is the ID-based counterpart of `add_edges()`. It is useful when edges are generated programmatically from node IDs (for example from `get_node_ids()` or the `id` column of a node DataFrame) and you want to be sure no value is accidentally interpreted as a label. Edges are added in list order, each with its own edge ID, and the call is recorded as a single step in the step log (see `steps`). Edges are added one at a time, so if an invalid ID is encountered part-way through the list, the edges before it have already been added when the error is raised. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Edge definitions to add. Each element can be: - A tuple of `(source_id, target_id)` with shared attributes applied. - A tuple of `(source_id, target_id, attrs_dict)` to override shared attributes. The dict is merged on top of `**shared_attrs=` and may also contain `"rel"` and `"weight"` keys to override `rel=` and `weight=` for that edge. Both IDs must be Python `int` values referring to existing nodes. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship type applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). Stored in the first-class `rel` column of the edge DataFrame. Default is `None`. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional numeric weight applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). Stored whether or not the graph was created with `weighted=True`. Default is `None`. [**shared_attrs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attributes applied to every edge (unless overridden per-edge). Each key becomes a column in the edge DataFrame. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any source or target is not an integer. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any source or target node ID does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Map labels to IDs once, then add a chain of edges by ID with a shared `rel`: ::: {#b8a39126 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D']) ids = { label: graph.get_id_from_label(label) for label in ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'] } graph.add_edges_by_id( [ (ids['A'], ids['B']), (ids['B'], ids['C']), (ids['C'], ids['D']), ], rel='link' ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: A dict as the third tuple element overrides the shared values for that edge only, so the Y-Z edge below is `"strong"` while X-Y keeps the shared `"weak"`: ::: {#27b9b0a2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(['X', 'Y', 'Z']) ids = { label: graph.get_id_from_label(label) for label in ['X', 'Y', 'Z'] } graph.add_edges_by_id( [ (ids['X'], ids['Y']), (ids['Y'], ids['Z'], {'rel': 'strong'}), ], rel='weak' ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Because the input is plain integer pairs, edge lists can be generated directly from node IDs. Here the five IDs returned by `get_node_ids()` are joined into a ring, giving one edge per node: ::: {#112b5738 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(range(1, 6)) node_ids = graph.get_node_ids() graph.add_edges_by_id( [(node_ids[i], node_ids[(i + 1) % len(node_ids)]) for i in range(len(node_ids))] ) graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
